headline: City and UEFA sign a Financial Fair Play settlement
summary: UEFA had questioned some of City's sponsorship agreements and whether the club met its break-even requirement. No findings were made. The two sides settled, with City accepting a fine, part of it suspended, and a reduced Champions League squad for 2014/15.

headline: Der Spiegel publishes leaked City emails
summary: The German outlet published internal club documents from the Football Leaks cache, alleging that money from City's owner had been presented as sponsorship income. City did not dispute that the emails were authentic, declined to comment on material it said had been hacked and stripped of context, and described the reporting as an attempt to damage its reputation.

headline: Premier League opens its investigation
summary: The League began investigating City's financial arrangements after the Der Spiegel reports. The investigation ran for four years.

headline: UEFA opens a formal investigation
summary: UEFA opened a formal investigation into whether City had broken its financial rules. City said it welcomed the chance to end the speculation and called the accusations false.

headline: UEFA investigator refers City for adjudication
summary: The chief investigator of UEFA's financial control body finished his investigation and referred the case to its adjudicatory chamber.

headline: CAS rejects City's bid to halt the UEFA case
summary: City had asked the Court of Arbitration for Sport in June 2019 to throw out UEFA's case before it was decided. CAS turned the request down.

sources.title: City timeline

headline: UEFA bans City from European competition for two seasons
summary: UEFA found serious breaches of its spending rules and a failure to cooperate with investigators, and imposed a two-season ban and a €30 million fine. City called the investigation flawed and appealed to CAS.

sources.title: Timeline: How Man City's Financial Case Went From Leaked Emails To Verdict

headline: CAS overturns the UEFA ban
summary: CAS upheld City's appeal, finding some of UEFA's allegations not proven and others time-barred. It lifted the ban and set a €10 million fine for failing to cooperate with investigators.

sources.title: Timeline: How Man City's Financial Case Went From Leaked Emails To Verdict

headline: Premier League charges City and refers the case to an independent Commission
summary: The League alleged more than 100 breaches of its rules: over the club's accounts and spending across 2009/10 to 2017/18, and over cooperation with its investigation from December 2018 up to the charges. City denied every charge and said the evidence supported its position.

summary: A three-member independent Commission began hearing the charges in private in London.

headline: Tribunal publishes its first award on the APT rules
summary: In a challenge brought by City, an arbitration tribunal found three aspects of the League's Associated Party Transaction rules unlawful, including the exclusion of shareholder loans. The League said City's wider challenge had largely failed.

headline: Clubs vote amended APT rules into force
summary: Premier League clubs approved new APT rules intended to fix the aspects the tribunal had found unlawful, including bringing shareholder loans into fair market value assessment.

summary: City began a second arbitration, this time against the rules adopted in November 2024.

headline: Tribunal rules the previous APT rules unenforceable
summary: The tribunal decided the three unlawful aspects could not be separated from the rest, making the previous APT rules unenforceable as a whole. It made no finding on the amended rules, which the League said remained in force.

headline: City and the Premier League settle the APT dispute
summary: Both sides agreed to end the arbitration. City accepted that the current APT rules are valid and binding. The settlement did not affect the separate Commission case.

headline: The Athletic reports the Commission's verdict
summary: The Athletic reported that City had been found guilty of all but one of the charges, four days before the League published the decision.

sources.title: Timeline: How Man City's Financial Case Went From Leaked Emails To Verdict

headline: Commission finds the charges proven, bar one
summary: The League published the Commission's redacted Core Decision. It found every charge proven except Charge 4(B). The Commission found that City ran a disguised funding scheme in which Abu Dhabi sponsors paid only part of their recorded fees and the club's owner paid the rest, overstating income by more than £830 million, and that the club exceeded both UEFA's and the League's spending limits once its accounts were restated. Sanction is to be decided at a separate hearing.

headline: City rejects the decision and says it will appeal
summary: City said it is innocent, called the decision legally and factually wrong, and said it will pursue the appeal routes open to it.
